clue.text: Concealed behind books

parts.note: behind, as in behind schedule, means late
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Something hidden away behind a row of books on a shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Something latent is present but hidden, not yet showing itself, so it is concealed.

clue.text: Fail to detain one caught giving sweetener

indicators.note: to detain is to hold someone inside, so these letters go within the word for fail

parts.note: to fail, in a contest, is to lose
one is the single letter A, as in a single item
CT is the scorecard abbreviation for caught in cricket

explanation.surface: Someone fails to keep a captured man who hands over a sugary substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Lactose is milk sugar, a natural sugar used in foods, so it counts as a sweetener.

clue.text: Article about soldier's figure

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the article's letters go round the soldier

parts.note: the is the definite article in grammar
RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for soldiers in crosswords

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a soldier's physique.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a number, and a number written down is a figure.

clue.text: Muse tends to be confused? It can't be helped!

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A poet's inspiring muse is prone to muddle, and there is nothing to be done about it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, short for 'needs must when the devil drives', says one has no choice, it cannot be avoided.

clue.text: Increase in position of shabby cinema

indicators.note: in places the word for a rise inside the word for position

parts.note: to fit something is to put it in position, as one fits a shelf
a leap is a sudden rise, as in a leap in prices

explanation.surface: A rise in someone's standing at a run-down picture house.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleapit is British slang for a grubby old cinema or theatre, supposedly infested with fleas.

clue.text: Precocious footballer

definitions.meaning: ... describes a child advanced or bold beyond its years

explanation.surface: A young football player who is gifted for his age.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward means advanced or presumptuous, and in football it names an attacking player in front of midfield.

clue.text: Patron of the arts in That Riviera Touch

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wealthy patron of the arts shows up in a glamorous film or show called That Riviera Touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, goddess of lyric and love poetry, a divine patron of an art form.

clue.text: Closely guarded pet tumbled over and over

parts.note: to pet an animal is to pat it
something that tumbled over and over has rolled

explanation.surface: A pampered pet animal fell head over heels, under close watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrolled area is watched over by guards going round it, so it is closely guarded.

clue.text: Squirm in Thursday's eruption

parts.note: TH is a standard abbreviation for Thursday
a rash is an eruption on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone writhing in discomfort at an outbreak of something on a Thursday.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrash about is to writhe or flail, which is close to squirming.

clue.text: Egoist twirled cigar

indicators.note: twirled means spun round, so the letters of the first word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed man twiddles his cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stogie is a long, thin, cheap cigar, originally American.

clue.text: Fish arrive for artisan

parts.note: carp is a freshwater fish
to enter a room is to arrive in it

explanation.surface: A fish turns up in place of a craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled woodworker, a kind of craftsman or artisan.

clue.text: Player fell after a collision, initially

indicators.note: after puts the hill word behind the letters before it
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of collision is used

parts.note: a fell is a northern English hill, and so is a tor

explanation.surface: A sportsman went down after a collision on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' looks like a verb (fell over), but it is the noun, a hill in northern England, giving TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor plays a part on stage, so a player is a common old word for one.

clue.text: Finished Sunday deliveries

parts.note: something finished is over

explanation.surface: Sunday post rounds have come to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, so the plural is groups of deliveries.

clue.text: Stunning girl — heartless and lustful

indicators.note: heartless means with the middle removed, so only the outside letters of girl stay

parts.note: amorous means full of sexual desire, lustful

explanation.surface: A striking young woman who is cold-hearted but passionate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunning and glamorous both describe striking, alluring good looks.

clue.text: Girl's prompt meeting eastern fugitive

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
a cue prompts an actor to speak

explanation.surface: A girl's quick meeting with someone from the east who is on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: An evacuee flees danger such as wartime bombing, so loosely a refugee or fugitive.

clue.text: A manner people initially take for making amends

parts.note: tone is the manner or style in which something is said
men means people, as in the men of a village

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of take is used

explanation.surface: Advice on the attitude people should adopt when they want to apologise.
explanation.definitionFit: Atonement is the act of putting a wrong right, which is what making amends means.

clue.text: Play with boy born in valley

indicators.note: in puts the letters for boy and born inside the word for valley

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England
B is an abbreviation for boy found in some dictionaries
B is the abbreviation for born, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Playing with a little boy born in a quiet country valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To dabble with something is to toy with it in a casual, non-serious way.

clue.text: Make one believe clothing's to be laundered

parts.note: a bra is an item of clothing
clothes waiting to be laundered are in the wash

explanation.surface: Persuading someone that their clothes need washing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between the item of clothing and the phrase 'in wash'.
explanation.definitionFit: To brainwash is to force someone by pressure to believe something, to make them believe it.

clue.text: Footwear worn by English stars

indicators.note: the footwear is worn by, so goes round, the letter for English

parts.note: boots are footwear

explanation.surface: Shoes or boots worn by English celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Boötes, the Herdsman, is a northern constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Pacify ten ewes in distress

indicators.note: in distress means upset or disordered, so the letters of the two preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Calming down ten anxious female sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweeten someone is to make them more agreeable, mollify them, so to pacify.

clue.text: Repairer retains bit of abdominal wind

indicators.note: retains means holds inside, so a letter goes within the word for repairer

parts.note: a mender repairs things

indicators.note: bit of here means just the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A repairman holds on to some stomach gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like the noun, flatulence, after 'abdominal', but it is the verb (rhymes with 'find'), to twist and turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that meanders follows a winding course, so to meander is to wind.

clue.text: Small car's no good in heavy industry

parts.note: a Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A small car is useless in the world of heavy manufacturing.
explanation.definitionFit: Mining, digging coal or ore out of the ground, is a classic example of heavy industry.

clue.text: Ruler ingests a compound that's active

indicators.note: ingests means takes inside, so the A goes within the word for ruler

parts.note: a regent rules in place of a monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch swallows some potent chemical substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used in a chemical reaction because it is reactive.

clue.text: Comment on evangelist

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
Mark is one of the four evangelists, the Gospel writers

explanation.surface: A remark about one of the Gospel writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is something said in passing, a comment.

clue.text: Standard is incessantly naive

parts.note: ever means always, incessantly, as in ever-present
green means inexperienced and naive

explanation.surface: A conventional norm that is endlessly simple-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a song that stays popular for years, which is also called an evergreen.

clue.text: German to criticise hard diagram

parts.note: to rap someone is to rebuke or criticise them
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A German sets out to tear apart a difficult chart.
explanation.definitionFit: A graph is a diagram showing how quantities relate.

clue.text: Nationalist in Jamaica is an assassin

parts.note: JA is the international abbreviation for Jamaica

explanation.surface: A political nationalist in Jamaica turns out to be a hired killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in stealth, often hired as a spy or killer.

clue.text: Unworldly domestic's short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so a letter is removed from the word for domestic

parts.note: native, as in native produce, means domestic, home-grown

explanation.surface: A household servant who lacks the time for worldly matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone naive is innocent and inexperienced, lacking worldly knowledge.

clue.text: Knight enters sector of the battlefield

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the knight's letter goes inside the word for sector

parts.note: an area is a sector or zone
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A mounted knight rides into one part of the field of battle.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a scene of conflict or struggle, as in the political arena, so a battlefield.

clue.text: I let Satan corrupt and torment

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or altered, so the letters of the three preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A confession: I allowed the Devil to deprave me and cause suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To tantalise is to torment with something desired but kept out of reach, as Tantalus was.

clue.text: Livingstone retained longing for the cookhouse

indicators.note: retained means held inside, so the longing goes within the first name

parts.note: Ken Livingstone was the first Mayor of London
an itch is a restless longing, as in an itch to travel

explanation.surface: The explorer Livingstone kept a yearning for the camp kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests David Livingstone the explorer; the wordplay needs Ken Livingstone, a former Mayor of London, for KEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cookhouse is a place where food is prepared, a kitchen, especially in a camp.

clue.text: Mad Hatter in danger

indicators.note: mad means crazed, so the letters of the following word are scrambled

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland is in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A threat is a source of possible harm, a danger or menace.
